item.title: LG TVs
item.description: At a time when home technology seems to have reached such a level of integration that it blends into our daily routines, becoming almost a natural extension of our lives, the controversy surrounding LG televisions has taken on significance that goes far beyond a mere technical issue, because it has brought back to the forefront of the discussion a topic that, despite having been around for years, rarely manages to emerge with the force needed to compel us to look at it without distractions. The relationship between what we believe we control and what, in reality, is watching us while we use it or even when we think we aren’t using it at all. Investigations conducted by Gamers Nexus, in collaboration with Level1Techs and several independent researchers, have in fact shown that certain models of LG OLED TVs do not merely collect information about what is displayed on the screen, but appear to be an integral part of a sort of continuous monitoring of the home’s digital environment as if the television had become an active node in a broader network, capable of observing, categorize, and interpret what is happening around it even when the screen is off, the device is in standby mode, or, in some cases, even disconnected from the network.

item.title: SING A BIT OF HARMONY
item.description: At a time when reflection on the relationship between technology and human sensibility seems to be taking on a prominent role in our lives, Sing a Bit of Harmony delicately weaves itself into this discourse, choosing to explore not so much the wonder of innovation as the complexity of the emotions that arise when an artificial intelligence, designed to assist and simplify daily life, begins to act with a curiosity reminiscent of that of human beings, as if the line between what is programmed and what is perceived suddenly becomes blurrier and harder to define.

item.title: NO DATE, NO SIGNATURE
item.description:
Each of us, at least once in our lives, has found ourselves amazed by how much we’ve come to love a movie that we’d always put aside to prioritize something more recent or better known.

“Doubt – A Case of Conscience” is a film that perfectly reflects this situation thanks to the deep sense of immersion the viewer experiences while following the lives of the various characters, whose stories gradually become intertwined without the use of directorial choices intended to shock the audience.

item.title: USA Today Co. & Palantir
item.description: There comes a moment, when observing the transformations taking place in the world of news, when one gets the impression that something is changing not only on the surface of the news, but in the very structure of the relationship between those who produce it and those who read it as if a slow and almost imperceptible shift were redrawing the rules of a pact that, for decades, we have taken for granted. The decision by USA Today Co. (the country’s largest newspaper chain) to form a partnership with Palantir (a company that for years has operated in contexts where data management is intertwined with government, military, and surveillance operations) seems to fit squarely within this kind of change, because it involves not just a business strategy or a technological upgrade, but touches on a deeper dimension: the one that defines the trust between a newspaper and its audience.

item.title: Chat Control
item.description:
Well, here we are… it’s finally happened.

Not because it was inevitable, but because the European Union continues to follow a certain pattern: when the interests of the most powerful come into play, the protection of rights and democracy seems to become a mere detail that can be sacrificed without too many qualms. In short, a script we now know all too well.

On 9 July, the European Parliament approved the exemption to the ePrivacy Regulation, the very same exemption that had been rejected in the spring. In practice, this gives big tech the green light to analyse private messages and emails in search of child sexual abuse material. On paper, it looks like a measure for the common good, but those concerned with digital privacy have been sounding the alarm for some time now. And not out of paranoia… because once a door like this is opened, closing it again becomes almost impossible.

item.title: PROJECT HAIL MARY
item.description:
“Project Hail Mary” has finally arrived on streaming platforms, making it perfect for anyone who didn’t get the chance to see it at the cinema. It’s one of those films that’s worth taking the time to watch, because behind its sci-fi adventure facade lies a human story and a unique way of portraying science.

The film is directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, a duo who have proven over the years that they can breathe life into even the riskiest projects. Here, they work closely with Ryan Gosling, who does not merely act but actively contributes to shaping the film’s tone. The film is based on the novel of the same name by Andy Weir, the author of The Martian.

item.title: BACKROOMS
item.description: Kane Parsons’s film debut, Backrooms, represents one of those rare moments when a grassroots phenomenon born in the depths of the internet and nurtured by a global community manages to make the leap to the big screen without completely losing its identity. The film, produced by A24 on a budget of ten million dollars, brings to the big screen the liminal and unsettling imagery that made the Backrooms creepypasta famous, and does so through the eyes of a very young filmmaker who, paradoxically, is already an integral part of the myth he is recounting. Parsons, in fact, is not merely a director called upon to interpret a trend, as he is one of its most influential creators, thanks to the series of short films published on YouTube that have earned him a global following.

item.title: XKeyscore
item.description: The XKeyscore program is one of the most pervasive and advanced pieces of software in the mass surveillance apparatus operated by the National Security Agency (NSA). In various classified documents and training materials, this tool is described as the cornerstone for collecting and analyzing information from computer networks, a process known in technical jargon as Digital Network Intelligence. Its most striking feature is its immense capacity to monitor global digital activity, covering nearly everything a user does on the internet. Through a simple interface, which mimics the operation of a standard web search engine, intelligence analysts can search numerous databases without needing a court order or prior review by superiors or courts. To launch a search, one simply enters a general justification into an online form, gaining immediate access to historical data and real-time intercepts. This complete absence of technical or legal safeguards within the software merely serves to confirm the validity of the controversial statements made in 2013 by the whistleblower Edward Snowden, who claimed that, from his desk as a private consultant for the NSA, he could have electronically intercepted anyone, from ordinary citizens to federal judges right up to the President of the United States, provided they had a simple email address.

item.title: FAST16
item.description:
SentinelOne recently published an in-depth analysis describing the discovery of a new cyber-sabotage framework called fast16, which forces us to reconsider the timeline of the development of cyber operations carried out by state-sponsored actors in the first half of the 2000s.

In particular, this malware, written in Lua and dating back to 2005, predates the infamous Stuxnet by at least five years – the so-called first digital weapon known to have physically targeted Iran’s nuclear infrastructure.

item.title: MILLENNIUM ACTRESS
item.description:
Millennium Actress is probably the least talked-about film by the late Satoshi Kon, but also one of his most profound and complex. Unlike his more famous works such as Paprika and Perfect Blue, this film demands greater attention from the viewer in order to grasp the plot and the underlying themes that run through it.

Kon eschews immediate spectacle and builds the narrative slowly, choosing to begin at the end and retrace the protagonist’s entire life. At first, one may feel a sense of disorientation, to the point of feeling overwhelmed by the events, but once you get a feel for the film’s rhythm, the story explodes with all its emotional power.

item.title: INNOVATION CONTEST
item.description:
I’ve recently heard some news which, without exaggerating, has completely changed the way I look at the future… for the better, for once!

I recently had the honour of representing Thevo, and in particular its research and development division, ThevoX, as part of the EDIH PRIDE project, which also organised the Innovation Contest for Hitachi Rail.

My friend (and colleague) Francesco De Micco and I, led by our Luigi Di Biasi, had the opportunity to present the “SrcProof” project directly to Hitachi Rail’s management, in a session reserved exclusively for the twenty projects selected from all the proposals received from across Italy. In short, not exactly a residents’ meeting.

item.title: ARCO
item.description: In his 2025 film, Ugo Bienvenu constructs a narrative universe populated by characters who, whilst set within a science-fiction context, embody themes that are profoundly human. Arco, Iris and the robot accompanying them are not merely characters serving the plot, but represent three complementary perspectives: the curious innocence of childhood, the emotional resilience of those growing up in a fragmented world, and the ability of machines to fill the voids left by human beings. Through these three figures, the film explores the relationship between technological progress, social fragility and the evolution of emotions, laying the foundations for a story that combines adventure and social commentary.

item.title: COSMIC PRINCESS KAGUYA
item.description:
The story is set in a future where technology has advanced to such an extent that it enables sensory and visual experiences that were once unimaginable, thanks to devices capable of immersing the user in a fully virtual world. In short, it is the much-coveted metaverse that the big tech companies are desperately trying to achieve.

The protagonist is Iroha Sakayori, a seventeen-year-old who spends her days juggling life as a model student with gruelling shifts at her part-time job to support herself. Her goal is to earn her mother’s respect (whose absence conveniently serves the film’s plot). Despite her hectic life, Iroha always manages to carve out a little time to escape into the virtual world and support her favourite VTuber idol, Runomi Yachio (basically an alternative version of our world’s Miku).

item.title: PROJECT NIMBUS
item.description:
The recent outbreak of war in Iran provides a new platform for showcasing the military supremacy of the United States and Israel. Their state-of-the-art technologies ensure total control of the battlefield. However, behind the automatic targeting systems lies an even more sophisticated infrastructure, the result of one of the most controversial technological projects of recent years.

Of all these, one that has caused the greatest public outcry is Project Nimbus, a joint venture agreement signed in 2021 between Google, Amazon, Microsoft and the State of Israel. The stated aim was to create a cloud infrastructure designed to provide the Israeli government with a range of automation services for managing bureaucracy. However, it is precisely behind this term that the true nature of the project is said to lie. According to numerous documents leaked by employees within the companies involved, the technologies provided by the American giants were allegedly used to develop a complex military system capable of identifying and eliminating Palestinian targets, accepting a high risk of civilian casualties.

item.title: DRIVE MY CAR
item.description: “But even if you think you know someone well, even if you love that person deeply, you cannot see completely into their heart. You will only feel hurt. But if you try hard enough, you should be able to see quite well into your own heart. So, in the end, what we should do is be honest with our hearts and accept them in a mature way. If you really want to see someone, the only option is to look at yourself directly and deeply.”

item.title: LIZ AND THE BLUE BIRD
item.description:
Liz and the Blue Bird is a 2018 film produced by Kyoto Animation and directed by Naoko Yamada (probably best known to most audiences for her work on the film The Voices of a Distant Bird), focusing on the relationship between Mizore and Nozomi, two close friends who are members of a high school music club.

Although the film is only a spin-off from the world of ‘Sound! Euphonium’, it is not necessary to have seen the series to understand the general context and fully enjoy the story. The introductory part, in fact, focuses exclusively on Mizore, a reserved and quiet girl who waits silently for her friend Nozomi (the perfect embodiment of the stereotype of the lively and popular girl among students) on the steps of their school.

item.title: THE SNOWMAN
item.description: The Snowman, directed by Dianne Jackson and based on Raymond Briggs’ illustrated book, is an animated short film that, despite its brevity, leaves a lasting impression on viewers. The story is simple: a child builds a snowman, which comes to life during the night. From that moment on, a friendship is born that leads them on an extraordinary adventure, culminating in the famous flight over snow-covered landscapes and illuminated cities, accompanied by the famous song ‘Walking in the Air’. It is a story that needs no words, because everything is conveyed through images and music, creating a universal language that speaks directly to the emotions.

item.title: CHAINSAW MAN - THE MOVIE: REZE ARC
item.description: Dear readers, please be advised that the following content may be seriously harmful to you if you have particular tastes, often justified with phrases such as ‘How can it be bad if it has made so much money??“ or ‘Tastes are subjective!”. so as a precaution, I recommend turning the page and relaxing with a new RAI series to return to your comfort zone. If, on the other hand, you consider yourself intrepid or crazy enough to want to continue, I welcome you to this new review, because what we are going to talk about is truly out of the ordinary and deserves to be told with care.

item.title: SOUL
item.description: There is a melody that vibrates beneath the surface of life, imperceptible but constant, made up of moments, emotions and silences. Soul attempts to capture it, to give it form and sound, through a narrative that intertwines jazz notes and otherworldly visions, philosophy and animation, lightness and depth. It is a film that is not content with simply telling a story, but seeks to explore the very meaning of existence, asking questions that we often avoid, but which have always tormented us.

item.title: ARETE HIME
item.description: There are films that don’t shout, don’t impose themselves, don’t try to please everyone. Princess Arete is one of them. Directed by Sunao Katabuchi and produced by Studio 4°C in 2001, it is a work that has chosen silence, slowness and depth. And for this reason, perhaps, it has never received the appreciation it deserves. But today, thanks to its free (albeit temporary) viewing on YouTube, we have a rare opportunity to rediscover it. And we should do so.

item.title: CINDERELLA THE CAT
item.description: There are films that manage to bend a myth without breaking it, to reinvent an archetype without dissipating its original magic. ‘Cinderella The Cat’ belongs to this select circle: a fairy tale tinged with the shadows of crime news, touching on the sharp edges of noir and delving into the pulsating and contradictory heart of Naples. No royal balls or golden pumpkins: Alessandro Rak, Ivan Cappiello, Marino Guarnieri and Dario Sansone’s Cinderella wanders barefoot among corroded walkways and corridors of the city’s underground. No royal balls or golden pumpkins: the Cinderella of Alessandro Rak, Ivan Cappiello, Marino Guarnieri and Dario Sansone wanders barefoot among corroded walkways and metal corridors inside the Megaride, a ship-world stranded in the harbour like a sleeping giant. That rusty steel is the funeral monument to a promise of progress never kept, the emblem of a bright future trapped in the meshes of corruption and abandonment.

item.title: KPOP DEMON HUNTERS
item.description:
If I had told you that the same studio behind ‘The Emoji Movie’ would produce a film about a K-pop band that defeats demons with music, you would probably have burst out laughing.

And I don’t blame you.

Yet ‘Kpop Demon Hunters’, released on Netflix in June 2025, has managed to establish itself as one of the platform’s most viewed titles, creating a surprisingly active and passionate community around it.

item.title: POMPO: THE CINÉPHILE
item.description:
‘Cinema is the most direct way to compete with God.’

Without meaning to, Fellini managed to sum up what this film is all about in a single sentence. The dream of an aspiring director turns into a passionate ode to the seventh art, told with the heart of someone who loves it deeply and the mind of someone who knows how to question it. Between surreal comedy and a structure that manages to alternate between comedy and drama, the viewer finds themselves immersed in a meta-cinematic film that shows the process of making a film, starting from dreams and ending with the birth of the work.

item.title: COLORFUL
item.description:
“What colour are you?”

Such a simple question, yet it encompasses a sea of meanings.

‘Colorful’, the animated film directed by Keiichi Hara (based on the novel by Eto Mori) and released in 2010, takes us on a delicate and profound journey on the theme of rebirth and self-acceptance.

The story begins in a rather unusual way: the viewer is enveloped in dark colours and the setting resembles a railway ticket office. Amidst this chaos, voice-over narration introduces us to the thoughts of a lost soul, disoriented and without identity.

item.title: POUPELLE OF CHIMNEY TOWN
item.description:
What does it mean to see beyond the smoke from the chimneys?

“Poupelle of the City of Chimneys” invites us to reflect on this and much more in a way that is as magical as it is moving.

Directed by Yūsuke Hirota and released in 2020, today we are discussing a Japanese film that presents itself as a modern fairy tale ready to enchant viewers with its fantastical setting and touching story of friendship, courage, and hope.

item.title: ETERNAL SUNSHINE OF THE SPOTLESS MIND
item.description:
When it comes to love stories that defy convention, ‘Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind’ stands out as a film that is truly one of a kind.

Directed by Michel Gondry and written by Charlie Kaufman, this 2004 masterpiece explores the complexities of human relationships through non-linear storytelling and a unique combination of emotions and philosophical reflections. Halfway between romantic drama and science fiction, the film tackles the themes of memory, regret and emotional resilience, offering the audience an intense and engaging experience.

item.title: THE BRUTALIST
item.description:
‘The Brutalist’ is Brady Corbet’s new film starring Adrien Brody, a duo that certainly needs no introduction.

This film is monumental in every respect, so much so that it seems like a blockbuster. The fact that it cost “only” ten million and was shot in a month makes it even more impressive, despite the fact that the Italian dubbing does not do it justice as well as the original version.

item.title: NEXTCLOUD: THE ULTIMATE SELF-HOSTED CLOUD SOLUTION
item.description:
In the current landscape of cloud productivity suites, Nextcloud stands out as one of the most interesting alternatives for those who want control, privacy and customisation. But what makes it truly special compared to the classic Google Workspace and Office 365?

Nextcloud is an open-source cloud storage platform that allows you to easily create a collaborative environment on your own server. This means that your data remains completely under your control, without having to rely on third parties. In fact, privacy and security are the pillars on which Nextcloud bases its offering.

item.title: TENSHI NO TAMAGO
item.description:
‘Tenshi no tamago’ is a 1985 Japanese animated film directed by Mamoru Oshii (also known for the famous ‘Ghost in the Shell’) which, since its theatrical release, has managed to surprise all viewers with its style reminiscent of a constantly moving pictorial fresco.

The plot centres on a mysterious little girl who carries a large egg with her as she travels through a post-apocalyptic world. Once she arrives in a rather “unusual” town, the girl meets a boy who wanders silently. From that moment on, the stories of the two characters intertwine and they keep each other company for the rest of the film.

item.title: AI AND MEDICINE: A WINNING COMBINATION?
item.description:
Lately, there has been increasing discussion about artificial intelligence, how it can revolutionise our lives, and what the future holds… even though the only innovation for the end user seems to be a new feature added to various products solely to increase sales.

Fortunately, there are also companies on the market such as Red Hat, a leader in the field of reliable open source solutions, which, despite some ethical stumbles since it was acquired by IBM, always strives to innovate and find real applications for new technologies.
